tip: Section 80C lets you claim deductions up to ₹1.5 lakh/year for PPF, ELSS, EPF, life insurance premiums, home loan principal, and more — but all of these share the same ₹1.5 lakh cap, they don't stack.
Section 80D allows a separate deduction (up to ₹25,000, or ₹50,000 if you or your parents are senior citizens) for health insurance premiums — independent of your 80C limit.
Section 80CCD(1B) gives an extra ₹50,000 deduction for NPS contributions, over and above the ₹1.5 lakh 80C limit — one of the few ways to get additional tax-deductible investment room.
Under the old tax regime, HRA exemption requires actual rent paid, a valid rent agreement, and landlord PAN details if annual rent exceeds ₹1 lakh — keep these documents ready before filing.

The new tax regime offers lower slab rates but removes most deductions and exemptions (80C, HRA, etc.). Whether old or new regime is better depends entirely on your specific deductions — it's worth calculating both.

Equity LTCG (gains on listed shares/equity funds held over 1 year) above ₹1.25 lakh in a financial year is taxed — check the current applicable rate each year, as these thresholds and rates have changed over time.
Interest earned on a savings account is eligible for a deduction up to ₹10,000/year under Section 80TTA (₹50,000 under 80TTB for senior citizens) — but only under the old tax regime.
ELSS funds have just a 3-year lock-in — the shortest among all Section 80C options — making them the fastest-unlocking way to combine tax saving with equity market participation.

Don't wait until March to start your tax-saving investments. Spreading your 80C SIP across the full financial year avoids both the cash-flow crunch and the rushed, poorly-chosen 'tax-saving' purchases common in February-March.

Form 26AS and the Annual Information Statement (AIS) show what the Income Tax Department already knows about your income and investments — cross-check them against your own records before filing to avoid mismatches.
If you switch jobs mid-year, collect Form 16 from both employers and combine the income when filing — relying on just one Form 16 can under-report your total taxable income.
Missing the ITR filing deadline doesn't just risk a penalty — it can also mean losing the ability to carry forward certain losses (like capital losses) to offset against future years' gains.

A home loan gives two separate tax benefits: principal repayment under Section 80C (within the overall ₹1.5 lakh cap) and interest paid under Section 24(b) (up to ₹2 lakh/year for a self-occupied property, old regime).
Capital losses on equity investments can be carried forward for up to 8 assessment years to offset future capital gains — but only if you file your ITR on time in the year the loss occurred.

Gifts received from specified relatives (parents, spouse, siblings, etc.) are generally tax-exempt in India, but gifts from non-relatives above ₹50,000 in a year can be taxable — know the distinction before large transfers.

TDS deducted on your fixed deposit interest isn't your final tax liability — it's an advance payment. You still need to report the full interest income and pay/claim refund on any shortfall/excess at filing time.
Advance tax applies if your total tax liability (after TDS) exceeds ₹10,000 in a financial year — relevant for freelancers, business owners, or anyone with significant capital gains or rental income.

Keep every investment proof (80C receipts, insurance premium receipts, donation receipts for 80G) organized through the year, not scrambled together in the final week — it prevents missed deductions and filing errors.

Donations to eligible charities under Section 80G can reduce taxable income, but the deduction percentage (50% or 100%) and any upper limit vary by the specific organisation — check its 80G certification before assuming the full amount qualifies.

If you're a freelancer or consultant, track and claim legitimate business expenses (internet, a portion of rent/utilities for home office, software subscriptions) against your professional income — many eligible deductions go unclaimed simply due to poor record-keeping.

A sudden salary jump mid-year (bonus, promotion) can push you into a higher slab — check your projected annual tax liability rather than assuming your current month's TDS deduction rate will hold for the full year.

Interest on an education loan is deductible under Section 80E (old regime) for up to 8 years, with no upper limit on the amount of interest claimed — a meaningful benefit often overlooked by borrowers.

Switching your mutual fund from a Regular Plan to a Direct Plan of the same scheme is usually treated as a redemption and fresh purchase for tax purposes — check the capital gains impact before switching, not after.

If you have capital losses, consider realizing some capital gains in the same financial year to offset against them (tax-loss harvesting) — but don't let the tax tail wag the investment dog; the underlying investment decision matters more.

Filing your ITR even when your income is below the taxable threshold can be useful — it creates a verifiable income record often needed for loan applications, visa processing, or claiming TDS refunds.

Interest earned on your PPF, EPF (up to the exempt contribution limit), and Sukanya Samriddhi Yojana is tax-free — among the few genuinely tax-free (not just tax-deferred) returns available to retail investors in India.

If you have rental income, remember you can claim a standard 30% deduction for repairs/maintenance regardless of actual expense, plus deduct home loan interest on that property — don't report gross rent as fully taxable.

Pre-validate your bank account on the income tax e-filing portal before filing — it's required for receiving any tax refund directly, and a mismatch in account details is a common reason refunds get delayed.

A Hindu Undivided Family (HUF) can be a separate tax entity with its own PAN and its own basic exemption limit and 80C benefits — a legitimate, often underused tool for certain family tax planning situations.

Life insurance maturity proceeds are tax-exempt under Section 10(10D) only if the premium paid in any year doesn't exceed a specified percentage of the sum assured — check this condition before assuming maturity payouts are automatically tax-free.
